title: Repo leaderboard
idea: Top 12 external repos ranked by PRs + issues + discussions, each with a stacked bar showing the mix (merged PRs, other PRs, issues, discussions) and the counts beside it. When the top repo has more than twice the runner-up's total, its bar is shortened and labelled with its true total and “not to scale”, so the other bars stay readable.

title: Owner leaderboard
idea: Top 12 organisations and people whose repos I contribute to, with repo count, a merged-PR gauge (merged of opened) and issue/discussion counts. Shows where PRs actually land versus where I mostly file issues.

title: Repos | owners, side by side
idea: Four headline numbers, then the top 10 repos and top 10 owners side by side. Each row has a 100% bar showing what kind of contribution it was (PR-heavy vs issue-heavy), so the number carries size and the bar carries character.

title: Dense table
idea: A compact 15-row table with explicit columns (stars, PRs, merged, issues, discussions, total, active years) and a totals row for all external repos. Nothing to decode: every number has a header.

title: Family roll-up
idea: Groups related GitHub owners into families (one vendor's several organisations) with the family total on top and member owners indented below, so a big vendor spread across many orgs shows up as one line.

title: Star tier vs my share
idea: Star-tier letters (S+ to C) that say what they mean: the left side is the repo’s popularity (stars, log scale, tier letter), the right side is what I contributed there. Big repos with small bars and small repos with big bars become obvious. When the top repo has more than twice the runner-up's total, its bar is shortened and marked “not to scale”.

title: Stacked bars + table
idea: The top 12 external repos as horizontal stacked bars (merged PRs, other PRs, issues, discussions) with the exact counts in aligned columns that double as the legend.

title: Treemap
idea: Every external repo as a tile sized by contributions, nested family → owner → repo, so the shape of the whole footprint (a few dominant blocks, a wide family spread, a long tail) is visible at a glance. The seven largest groups get colours.

title: Donut + ranked legend
idea: Share of all upstream work by family or owner as a donut (seven largest groups plus everyone else), next to a ranked table with avatars, share and a PR/issue breakdown per group.

title: Stars vs involvement
idea: Each repo plotted by stars (log) against my contributions (log), coloured by whether code landed; shows depth in mid-size projects versus drive-by issues on giant ones. Labels go to the 7 repos with most contributions, then the highest stars × contributions among repos with at least 3, up to 11 in all, each placed where it overlaps no other label and no other labelled repo's dot.

title: Waffle
idea: One square per contribution, grouped by family or owner, with merged PRs solid and everything else faded, so volume and code-vs-reports read together. Very large totals switch to one square per few contributions so the grid always fits.

title: Activity over time
idea: Monthly contributions as a stacked area by family or owner, showing peaks and how the mix shifts between groups. It starts in the first year holding at least 5% of all activity; anything earlier is counted in the footnote.

title: Big numbers
idea: Four large, labelled headline figures for upstream work (PRs opened, merged, issues, owners), with the five most active owners underneath. Reads in one glance.

title: Terminal table
idea: A fake `upstream --top 12` command that types itself out and prints an aligned monospace table of the top repositories (language, stars, PRs, merged, issues, discussions), with a totals line.

title: Receipt
idea: A till receipt itemised by owner, with company families (several orgs under one brand) rolled into one line, a breakdown under each item and a grand total of every upstream PR, issue and discussion. The barcode is the last 53 weeks of activity.

title: Git log
idea: The latest upstream pull requests (merged and open; closed-unmerged ones are hidden) as a `git log --graph` timeline: date, repo#number, title and diffstat, so visitors see what you are working on right now.

title: In brief
idea: A short paragraph written from the data: totals, merge count, the top three repositories, the biggest company family (the one with several owners and the most contributions) and this year's leading repository, with every figure set in bold.

title: Index
idea: A typeset back-of-book index of the 30 most active owners, alphabetical with letter heads and dotted leaders to the contribution count. Calm, dense and easy to scan for a name.

title: Orbit
idea: You at the centre, every org or user you contributed to on a ring by how much (40+, 16–39, 9–15, 6–8), avatar size by total; dotted lines join owners of one family from the family list.

title: Avatar mosaic
idea: A treemap wall of avatars: each tile’s area is that org’s or user’s share of all upstream contributions, with the count on every tile, a PR/issue breakdown on the big ones, and one tile pooling everyone with 5 or fewer.

title: Repo × month heatmap
idea: The 12 upstream repos with the most contributions as rows and every month from January of the year the earliest of them started as columns, with a bar strip of all upstream activity per month on top, so bursts and long-running work both show.

title: Swimlanes
idea: One lane per top upstream repo in the order I started on it: a line from first to last contribution and a dot per month sized by that month’s count, so the hand-offs between projects read like a timeline.

title: Skyline
idea: Each building is one of the top 15 orgs or users, its height is the number of contributions and its floors split them into merged PRs, other PRs, issues and discussions, on a real scale with round-number gridlines.

title: Year calendar + top upstream
idea: The familiar 53-week contribution calendar beside the five upstream repos with the most contributions in the months that window touches, so the year’s rhythm and where the upstream part went sit together.

title: Four stat tiles
idea: Upstream PRs, merge rate, repositories and owners as four equal 198px tiles in one 840px strip, each with a tiny supporting visual (activity per year over the last four years, merge ring, top languages, top-owner avatars). Tiles rise in with a short staggered entrance.

title: Owner badge strip
idea: Shields.io-style pills, one per top owner (up to 24) with its avatar and a contribution count. Reads as a compact "who I contribute to" line and wraps to the README width.

title: Repo spotlight
idea: One repository in focus: avatar, stars, language, PR/issue/discussion breakdown and a monthly activity histogram over the active span. It picks the repository with the most contributions among those not owned by the top owner. 410px, so two sit side by side.

title: Combined dashboard
idea: Everything in one card: KPI strip, top owners with stacked contribution bars, top repositories as a compact table, and a weekly activity strip for the last 12 months. Bars grow in on load.

title: Primer repository list
idea: Looks like a native GitHub list: an issues-style header with octicon tabs and counters, Box rows with blue repo links, language/owner label pills, dates and per-type counts.

title: Ecosystems (narrow)
idea: A 420px card grouping work by vendor family (one brand spread across several orgs) with member-org avatars, scaled stacked bars and a written breakdown. Built to pair with another narrow card.

title: Contribution Sankey
idea: A Sankey from you through families and owners to repositories, band height proportional to PRs + issues + discussions. The 7 biggest groups and 10 biggest repos are named; the rest are merged into one node per column so every band still adds up.

title: PR outcomes
idea: An alluvial from the families and owners you opened PRs with to how they ended: merged, still open or closed without merging (GitHub's purple, green and red). The 8 groups with the most PRs are named with their merge rate; the rest share one node.

title: Metro map
idea: A subway map where each line is one of the 6 families or owners with the most repositories (ties by contributions), and its stations are up to 8 of its biggest repos in order of first contribution, sized by PRs + issues + discussions. Shows breadth: where you branched out, not just where you contributed most.

title: Rank by year
idea: A bump chart of the top 8 families and owners in each calendar year (from repos' monthly counts), so you can see who rose, who faded and who stayed. Years with fewer than 10 contributions are left out (the latest 6 are shown); the 7 biggest over those years get colour, the rest stay grey.

title: First contact
idea: How the network grew: owners grouped by the year of your first PR, issue or discussion with them (earliest repos[].first), with a bar for how many were new that year, the running total, and the biggest of each year's cohort. Leading years that each brought under 5% of owners fold into one column; at most 6 columns.

title: Contribution tree
idea: A half-radial tree: you at the root, the 8 biggest families and owners on the inner ring, and up to 4 of each one's biggest repos as leaves, with stroke width proportional to PRs + issues + discussions. A compact picture of how the work branches out.

title: Trading cards
idea: The top three owners as collectible cards: avatar art, a stat block of PRs merged, PRs, issues and discussions, and a rarity tier from the total stars on the repos contributed to (thresholds printed in the legend).

title: Achievement medals
idea: A sheet of eight medals, each computed from the data (most merged PRs in one repo, repos in one family, owners, issues, languages, stars, longest run, merge rate) and struck in bronze, silver or gold against thresholds printed under it.

title: Periodic table of owners
idea: The top 54 owners laid out in the first five periods of the periodic table: atomic number = rank, a unique two-letter symbol from the login, mass = PRs + issues + discussions. Families colour their owners like element groups; other owners are grouped as organizations or users.

title: Passport stamps
idea: A passport page with one ink stamp for each of the top 12 owners by contributions, dated with my first PR, issue or discussion there and placed in order of that date; shape, ink and tilt come from a hash of the login so they never change between renders.

title: Ticket stubs
idea: The top six repositories by contributions as admission tickets: the repo is the show, its stars and language the billing, PRs, merged, issues and discussions the printed fields, and the stub keeps the rank and total. The coloured edge is the repo's language colour.

title: Arcade high scores
idea: A retro arcade high-score table in a bitmap font drawn from SVG pixels: the top ten owners ranked by score (PRs + issues + discussions in their repos) with PRs, merged PRs, issues and discussions as extra columns; the header shows the player, the top score and how many owners are on the board.

title: Family deep-dive
idea: One family in depth: its member orgs, its repositories and the PR, issue and discussion split, so a cluster like AWS reads as one relationship. Rule: the family with the most contributions (a lone top owner if no families are defined); up to 8 owners and 10 repositories, the rest summed.

title: Selected repositories
idea: A headline tile per notable repository, led by its total contribution count, each with its PR, issue and discussion counts and a monthly activity strip. Rule: the top 5 repositories with at least 1,000 stars by contributions; if fewer than 3 qualify, the biggest remaining repositories fill up to 3.

title: Merge funnel
idea: What happens to the PRs I open upstream: opened, decided (merged or closed), merged, with the drop at each step, then the same split for each family next to everyone else. Rule: families ranked by PRs opened, up to 7, the remaining owners summed in one row.

title: Year in review
idea: A wrapped-style story of one year upstream: contributions per month, the busiest month, the top repository and family, owners and repositories contributed to for the first time, and the same months a year earlier. Rule: the year of the snapshot, or the latest year with activity if it has none; a partial year is compared with the same months of the year before.

title: Milestones
idea: A timeline of firsts and round numbers derived from the data: the first upstream contribution, the 100th and 500th, the 10th and 100th repository, the first 1k+ and 10k+ star repository, the first contribution to the biggest family, the busiest month, on a cumulative curve. Rule: at most 12 milestones, firsts kept before round numbers; month-only dates come from monthly counts; months without contributions are drawn at a fifth of the width on the axis.

title: Family versus family
idea: The three biggest families side by side: total and share, each contribution kind on one shared scale with the leader in bold, merge rate, active span, top repository and member owners. Rule: the top 3 families by contributions; when there are fewer than 3, the biggest independent owners fill the remaining columns as groups of one.
